thread:
oliver: Quick heads-up — ran a TP workload repro and saw a 2.8x latency tail when we hit small-message all-reduce window. Throwing it here.

maria: Can you paste the flame/gprof output? Is this during warmup or steady-state?

oliver: Steady-state. Flame shows long hangs in `generic_reduce_kernel` after the kernel-selector falls back. Kernel selector log:
```
[kernel-select] model: tp-gpt-7b, seq=128, msg=512B -> selected: optimized_allreduce if msg>=2KB else generic_reduce_kernel
```
Fall back happens because our `msg_size` heuristics mis-class the coalesced chunk size (KV cache inflight fragmentation).

kevin: Ugh. So small message path ends up using a kernel that doesn't overlap comm/compute well. Any NCCL algorithm info?

oliver: NCCL reports ring algorithm for those sizes, but topology hinting later switches to tree for mixed sizes. The switch point seems noisy. Logs:
```
[nccl] algo=ring msg=600B -> expected latency 0.9ms
[nccl] algo=tree msg=600B -> latency 2.1ms
```

sam: Are we sure the message is actually 600B on wire? KV cache fragmentation + batching heuristics could produce many tiny fragments that land as separate reductions.

oliver: Good call. I instrumented the coalescer: it emits 3 fragments of ~200B each for some micro-batches. Kernel selector uses the single-frag size rather than aggregated inflight size.

maria: That's the bug then. Kernel selector should consider the effective allreduce payload (sum of inflight frags per tensor) not per-frag size. Quick patch idea: compute `effective_msg = min(total_inflight_for_tensor, configured_chunk_threshold)` and use that for kernel selection.

kevin: Also worth trying: nudge NCCL to prefer ring for those cases by setting `NCCL_ALGO=ring` in canary. If tree spikes are bigger, forcing ring might help until selector is fixed.

infra-bot: Canary deploy queued: infra/canaries/tp-allreduce-kernselect-2026-03-18

sam: Two quick experiments:
1) Force ring via env var on canary nodes.
2) Change kernel selector to use aggregated inflight size (local build; tiny test harness attached).

oliver: Results from (1): tail latency dropped ~25% but median similar. From (2): tail dropped ~60%, throughput steady. Patch diff attached in PR #4321.

maria: Nice. Any regression risk? Does aggregated-size selection cause worse perf for genuinely small genuine-msg tensors (lots of tensors with single small frag)?

kevin: We ran a synthetic sweep: when tensors are independently small and non-coalescable, selector keeps using generic kernel — because aggregated inflight for each tensor is still small. Only collated cases flip to optimized kernel. No negative regressions found in our microbench.

sam: Next steps proposal:
- ship kernel selector fix behind config flag
- canary ring-for-small override for 48 hours
- add a metric: `selector_decision:reason` to trace why we chose a kernel (frag_size vs aggregated)
- follow-up: consider coalescer change to avoid 3x 200B fragments (batching window tweak)

oliver: I'll open the canary rollout PR and add the `selector_decision` trace. PRs: #4321 (selector), #4322 (canary env). I'll also attach the reproducer command: `./bench_tp_allreduce --gpus 8 --seq 128 --batch 4 --kv-frag=200` — reproduces locally.

maria: Great. Add a short playbook for oncall in case the canary causes regressions (how to revert env var / flag).

kevin: Thanks team. This explains the weird latency cliff we saw last week. Good catch, and kudos on the quick root cause.

oliver: +1. I'll invite infra to the rollout PR for scheduling.

infra-bot: deploy status: canary started on 3 nodes; health checks OK.

sam: I'll follow up with an experiment to adjust coalescer window heuristics next week.

maria: Closing loop: we'll merge selector fix behind flag after canary verification, then enable globally in 48h if no regressions.

oliver: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
